कष् {vI.v} {c1c} U. (कषति-ते, कषित)
1 To
rub, scratch, scrape; समूलकाषं कषति
Sk; Bk. 3. 49.
--2 To test, try, rub
on a touch-stone (as gold); छदहेम
कषन्निवालसत्कषपाषाणनिभे नभस्तले
N. 2. 69.
--3 To injure, destroy.
--4 To
itch.
--5 To leap. {vII.v} {c10c} P. (काषयति)
To hurt.

कस् {vI.v} {c1c} P. (कसति, कसित) To
move, go, approach. {vII.v} {c2c} A. (कस्ते
or कंस्ते)
1 To go.
--2 To destroy.

काश् {c1c} {c4c} A. (काश-श्य-ते, काशित)
1 To shine, look brilliant or
beautiful; R. 10. 86, 7. 24; Ku. 1. 24;
Bk. 2. 25; Śi. 6. 74.
--2 To appear, be
visible; नैव भूमिर्न च दिशः प्रदिशो वा
चकाशिरे Mb.
--3 To appear, or look like.

कास् {c1c} A. (कासते, कासित)
1 To
shine,; see काश्.
--2 To cough,
make a sound indicating any disease.

कश्यपः a. Having black teeth.
--पः
1 A tortoise.
--2 A sort of fish.
--3 A kind of deer.
--4 N. of a
Ṛṣi, the husband of Aditi and
Diti, and thus the father both of gods
and demons, (so called because he
drank कश्य ‘liquor;’ cf. कश्यपस्तस्य
पुत्रोऽभूत् कश्यपानात् स कश्यपः । Mārk. P.)
[He was the son of Marīci, the son of
Brahmā. He bears a very important
share in the work of creation.
According to Mahābhārata and other accounts,
he married Aditi and 12 other
daughters of Dakṣa, and begot on Aditi
the twelve Ādityas. By his other
twelve wives he had a numerous and
very diversified progeny: serpents,
reptiles, birds, demons, nymphs of
the lunar constellation. He was thus
the father of gods, demons, men,
beasts, birds and reptiles-in fact
of all living beings. He is therefore
often called Prajāpati].
--Comp.
--नंदनः an epithet of Garuḍa.

1 N. of a celebrated
sage.
--2 N. of Kaṇāda.
--3 An
epithet of Aruṇa.
--पी The earth;
तानपि दधासि मातः काश्यपि यातस्तवापि च
विवेकः Bv. 1. 68.
--पं Flesh.
--Comp.
--नंदनः {1} an epithet of Garuḍa. {2}
N. of Aruṇa. {3} a god. {4} a demon.

[1] Correction submitted by on 20170214. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/Cologne/issues/157. note: kaSA is a headword, and alternate of kazA.

कषाय a.
1 Astringent; Ś. 2.

--5 Brown.

1
